    Remark 5.7: individual bricks #

    Quotients. Special biserial path data on A induce special biserial path data on every quotient A ⧸ J by a two-sided ideal: keep the vertices and arrows that survive in A ⧸ J (PathData.survData, PathData.quot_isSpecialBiserial).

    Individual bricks. A nonsimple brick M over a special biserial algebra has a brick submodule or quotient of dimension one less as soon as its faithful quotient is representation-finite (hasSmallerBrick_of_faithful, remark_5_7): Theorem A applies over the faithful quotient, which is special biserial and brick-finite, and Lemma 2.4 lifts the result.

    For right Λ-modules, that is left Λᵐᵒᵖ-modules, the faithful quotient Λ / ann_Λ(M) acts through Λᵐᵒᵖ ⧸ ann(M); its right modules are the left modules over this quotient.

        theorem BrickAccessibility.remark_5_7 (k : Type u) [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k] (Λ : Type u) [Ring Λ] [Algebra k Λ] [FiniteDimensional k Λ] (hsb : Statement.IsSpecialBiserial k Λ) (M : Type u) [AddCommGroup M] [Module Λᵐᵒᵖ M] [Module k M] [IsScalarTower k Λᵐᵒᵖ M] [FiniteDimensional k M] (hM : Statement.IsBrick Λᵐᵒᵖ M) (hns : ¬IsSimpleModule Λᵐᵒᵖ M) (hrf : IsRepFinite (Λᵐᵒᵖ ⧸ Module.annihilator Λᵐᵒᵖ M)) :
        Statement.HasSmallerBrick k Λ M

        Remark 5.7. An individual nonsimple brick M over a special biserial algebra Λ has a brick submodule or quotient of dimension one less whenever its faithful quotient is representation-finite. Here M is a right Λ-module, so the faithful quotient acts as Λᵐᵒᵖ ⧸ ann(M).
